title: How to Compress Password-Protected e-Aadhaar and Bank PDFs for Upload
metaDescription: Learn why portals reject password-protected e-Aadhaar and bank statement PDFs, how to safely remove the password, and how to compress them under 200KB for online forms.
author: Zcompressor Engineering
heroHeadline: How to compress password-protected e-Aadhaar & bank PDFs for online upload.
heroDescription: Government scholarship and exam portals instantly reject password-protected PDFs. Here is how to unlock your e-Aadhaar or bank statement locally and compress it under 200 KB.

sections.heading: 1. Why government portals reject password-protected files.
body: When you download an official electronic document—such as an e-Aadhaar from UIDAI or a bank account statement—it comes encrypted with a mandatory user password (usually your name and birth year).

Government portals (NSP, UPSC, JoSAA, SSC, State PSCs) employ automated backend verification bots to ingest documents, generate preview thumbnails, and verify identity details. These automated crawlers cannot prompt for or enter passwords; encountering an encrypted PDF causes the portal upload parser to immediately fail.

sections.heading: 2. The official e-Aadhaar password formula.
body: For e-Aadhaar PDFs downloaded from the UIDAI portal, the universal password consists of 8 characters: the first 4 letters of your name as printed on Aadhaar in CAPITAL letters, followed by your 4-digit Year of Birth.
For example, if your name is SURESH KUMAR and your birth year is 1998, your PDF unlock password is SURE1998. If your name has only 3 letters (e.g., RIA), the format is RIA1998.

sections.heading: 3. How to safely remove password encryption on your device.
body: Never upload your password-protected Aadhaar card to random online 'PDF password remover' websites. Sending your personal password and biometric identity card to untrusted servers compromises your personal security.

Instead, unlock it natively on your device: open the PDF in Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, or Apple Safari on your computer or phone, enter your password to view the document, click the 'Print' button, choose 'Save as PDF' (or 'Microsoft Print to PDF') as the printer destination, and save the new unencrypted PDF file.

sections.heading: 4. Compressing the unlocked document under 200 KB.
body: Once unlocked, an e-Aadhaar PDF typically measures between 400 KB and 1.5 MB due to high-resolution QR codes and UIDAI graphic letterheads. However, scholarship portals like NSP, UP Scholarship, and MahaDBT enforce a strict 200 KB ceiling.
Upload the unlocked PDF to Zcompressor and select the 200 KB target. Zcompressor compresses the visual assets while keeping the QR code and your 12-digit Aadhaar number razor-sharp.

faq.q: Can I upload a password-protected PDF to the NSP scholarship portal?
faq.a: No. The National Scholarship Portal (NSP) will reject encrypted PDFs with an 'Invalid File' or 'Cannot Parse Document' error. You must remove the password before uploading.

faq.q: Does Zcompressor store my Aadhaar card details?
faq.a: No. Zcompressor operates 100% locally in your web browser. Your document is processed entirely in your device memory and never transmitted to any external server.
